admission.justification: The setup operation and installer must agree on initialization, attributed baseline and truthful state handover; the Architect/Curator continuation owns actual foundation authoring in its real task.

applicability: First-hour Bootstrap/install setup of a new memory root and its handover to the Architect-owned foundation task; already-committed memory retains the stated ordering exception.
conditions: Setup initializes the memory root before baseline adoption, reads baseline status before and after adoption, and authors no onboarding or knowledge.
After reporting the knowledge state, setup tells the developer to start the Architect; the Architect opens the real task and its Curator authors through that task’s admitted writer and enclosure.
A new memory root needs the baseline commit before foundation authoring; memory that already has a commit may reach foundation before onboarding or baseline adoption.
exclusions: Making onboarding mandatory for every foundation or baseline.
Fabricating a task, worktree or enclosure merely to satisfy a writer argument list, or using a taskless authoring session in place of the real Architect task.
Bootstrap seat authoring onboarding or knowledge, starting another role, or owning ordinary Git/closeout transactions.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_bootstrap_converted_onboarding.py::test_bootstrap_skill_texts_state_the_fixer_and_the_order; composed journey test (init, cards, fixer, status, adopt, reads, refusal)

statement: New-repository setup runs memory_init and attributed baseline adoption without authoring onboarding or running its fixer, reports the knowledge state and tells the developer to start the Architect; the Architect opens the regular foundation task whose Curator authors against the required memory commit.
